subject: Information Theory
title: Radio Waves as Channels
description: Learn Radio Waves as Channels in one minute.

hook.text: Marconi sent the letter S across the Atlantic in 1901. Radio proved that air itself could be an information channel.

buildup.text: Radio waves carry information by modulating frequency, amplitude, or phase. The air is the transmission medium.

discovery.text: Shannon's formula applies: the capacity of a radio channel depends on bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio.

twist.text: Spectrum is finite. Every wireless device shares the same electromagnetic medium. It's a shared, noisy, crowded channel.

climax.text: The entire wireless industry—phones, WiFi, satellites—is an exercise in approaching Shannon's limit on radio channels.

punchline.text: Air carries data. Shannon's limit says how much.

quiz.question: What determines the capacity of a radio channel?
